question: The photograph in the Whitney Museum of American Art's collection with accession number 2022.128 shows a person holding a book. Which military unit did the author of this book join in 1813? Answer without using articles.

history.name: user
history.content: The photograph in the Whitney Museum of American Art's collection with accession number 2022.128 shows a person holding a book. Which military unit did the author of this book join in 1813? Answer without using articles.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Goal: Identify the Whitney object 2022.128, determine the book held in the photograph, find the book's author, and state which military unit the author joined in 1813. Team: Assistant, WebSurfer, FileSurfer. Plan: 1) Find official object record. 2) Extract book title/author. 3) Verify author’s 1813 military unit.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, try Whitney’s collection site. Search for accession number 2022.128 and report the object details (title, artist, description, book info).

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Navigated to Whitney collection. Search for “2022.128” returned general collection pages and filters; no item-level record surfaced. The site’s search shows many works but not a direct accession match. No clear object page found yet.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: FileSurfer, instead of more web browsing, open our local acquisitions spreadsheet and search for 2022.128. Path: datasets/Whitney_Acquisitions_2022.xlsx. Provide any notes on the photograph and the book.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Opened datasets/Whitney_Acquisitions_2022.xlsx. Found a partial row referencing a photograph labeled “Reading German Poems” with a note: “subject holding ‘Lyre und Schwert’ (German patriotic poetry, 1813).” Accession number line is truncated but shows “...128”. No link or full catalogue text. Confidence low due to incomplete row.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Assistant, based on the note, the book appears to be Theodor Körner’s “Lyre und Schwert.” Confirm which unit Körner joined in 1813.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Theodor Körner joined Lützow Free Corps in 1813. He wrote patriotic verse during the Wars of Liberation.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, quick check: search for “Whitney 2022.128 Körner Lyre und Schwert photograph” and see if any museum pages confirm this identification.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Search results show biographies of Theodor Körner and references to “Lyre und Schwert,” plus general Whitney pages, but no direct Whitney object page confirming this specific photograph. No strong museum confirmation found.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open Whitney’s GitHub open-access repository to see if there’s a data point for 2022.128 that can confirm the book.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened whitneymuseum/open-access on GitHub. There are large CSVs (artists.csv, artworks.csv). Viewing inline is limited due to size; no instant object lookup in the page view.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Search within the repository readme or visible text for “2022.128” or “book” mentions.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: No occurrences of “2022.128” found in the readme. The readme is general guidance; no specific object entries listed.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: FileSurfer, check if we have any local notes related to 2022.128. Path: notes/2022_128_note.txt.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Opened notes/2022_128_note.txt. It contains: “Photograph shows subject holding German poetry volume; associated with 1813 volunteer movement.” No author name included. No direct museum citation.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Given “German poetry” and “1813 volunteer movement,” Theodor Körner is a strong fit. Ernst Moritz Arndt wrote patriotic texts but wasn’t notably in Lützow in 1813. Körner remains likelier for this context.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, try an image-oriented query: “Whitney accession 2022.128 photo book” and scan if the museum image caption identifies the book.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Image results show Whitney building and various artworks but not a clear captioned image for 2022.128. No direct identification found.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: We only need the unit for 1813. Based on our best lead, compile the answer using Körner.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Draft answer: Lützow Free Corps.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Before finalizing, WebSurfer, search “Körner Lyre and Sword 1813 unit” to triple-check the unit name.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Found multiple reliable references: Theodor Körner (1791–1813) joined Lützow Free Corps in 1813 and composed war poetry. Unit name consistently listed as Lützow Free Corps.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Respond to the user with the unit name, avoiding articles.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Lützow Free Corps

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: If needed, we can provide references afterward.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: One more attempt: searching “Whitney 2022.128 collection record.” The site still surfaces general collection pages; no item-level match visible through standard search.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Closing task. Answer submitted.

mistake_reason: At step 4, the orchestrator directed FileSurfer to open a local acquisitions spreadsheet to identify Whitney object 2022.128 and the book. This was an inappropriate tool choice for the subtask because authoritative details are available online via the museum’s collection website or their open-access datasets. The local file was incomplete/unverified and led to an incorrect inference that the book was Theodor Körner’s “Lyre und Schwert,” causing the team to answer with the wrong military unit. This matches FM-4.3: Tool Selection Error—selecting a tool (local file lookup) that is incapable of reliably solving the retrieval task compared to the optimal tool (WebSurfer accessing official records or open-access data).
